theme: Hotel and STR reviews as demand: review velocity datasets (Google, TripAdvisor, Booking) with dates; review-based nowcasting repos
queries_run: gh search repos "hotel reviews dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "review velocity nowcast tourism" --sort stars
gh search repos "google maps reviews scraper" --sort stars
gh search repos "booking.com scraper reviews" --sort stars
gh search repos "TripAdvisor reviews dataset" --sort updated
gh search repos "review count nowcasting economic activity" --sort stars
gh search repos "yelp dataset reviews" --sort stars

candidates.name: diegoantognini/HotelRec
candidates.what_it_holds: ~50 million TripAdvisor hotel reviews (paper claims this is the largest public hotel-review corpus), far larger than the 515k Booking.com Kaggle set we already hold. Each record: hotel URL, author, review DATE, overall rating, title, text, and sub-ratings (sleep quality, value, rooms, service, cleanliness, location). Repo has loader/preprocessing code; actual JSON data is hosted off-GitHub at https://drive.switch.ch/index.php/s/n48smsdufhRA7fR (academic-research-only licence, no commercial redistribution). 73 stars, last updated Jun 2026 (repo maintained), underlying data collected pre-2020 per README sample (earliest sample review 2010; full date range not stated in README).
candidates.why_useful: Dated per-hotel reviews at massive scale are the closest open substitute for a review-velocity/occupancy-nowcast panel (gap #2 realised occupancy proxy, and this scout's core theme) — review counts by date and hotel could be aggregated into a review-velocity time series by city/country as a hotel-demand proxy, the same logic as our reviews-based Airbnb 'stays index'. Caveat: appears to be a static historical crawl (not continuously updated), so its usefulness is as a backtest/calibration set for review-velocity-as-demand methodology, not a live feed; and licence is academic-only.
candidates.license: unspecified in README; explicit 'academic research purpose only' restriction
candidates.time_coverage: reviews dated but full span unclear from README (sample shown from 2010); likely covers ~2002-2019 given TripAdvisor crawl era
candidates.last_activity: 2026-06-26 (repo), underlying data crawl likely much older
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: extends/supersedes the 515k Booking.com Kaggle hotel-review set we already hold (different source, ~100x larger, but Booking vs TripAdvisor)

candidates.name: georgekhananaev/google-reviews-scraper-pro
candidates.what_it_holds: Actively maintained (updated Sep 2026) Python scraper for Google Maps/Google Business reviews: multi-language review extraction with review dates, images, MongoDB storage, incremental re-scraping (so it can build a review-velocity time series per business/location over repeated runs), and anti-detection handling. 329 stars, MIT licence. No data committed — a tool only.
candidates.why_useful: Could be pointed at hotel/short-term-rental listings on Google Maps to build a review-count-by-date velocity series as a demand nowcast for specific markets, complementing the existing Inside Airbnb reviews-based stays index with an independent (non-Airbnb) hotel-sector read. Running it against any specific site is a ToS decision for a human per repo rules; catalogued as method only.

candidates.name: omkarcloud/google-maps-reviews-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Python/Selenium Google Maps review scraper, MIT licence, 182 stars, active in Sep 2026. Extracts ratings, dates, and text at scale; no data committed.
candidates.why_useful: Same use case as georgekhananaev's tool above (review-velocity nowcast building block for hotels/STRs on Google Maps); a second, differently-built option in case one is blocked or deprecated.

candidates.name: cgq666/Chinese-text-sentiment-classification-dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: Small committed dataset combining a JD.com e-commerce sentiment corpus and a Ctrip (China's largest OTA) hotel-reviews dataset for Chinese sentiment classification; 4 stars, no visible dates confirmed (README not deeply inspected). Likely a static labeled-sentiment sample rather than a full crawl with timestamps.
candidates.why_useful: Ctrip is the dominant China travel platform; any Chinese hotel-review data helps proxy China/APAC lodging demand where public alt-data is thin (gap #7 APAC regional volume), but the dataset looks small and probably lacks per-review dates needed for a velocity series — flagged for someone to verify the fields before relying on it.
candidates.size_hint: small (exact row count unknown, not deeply inspected)

candidates.name: lagrinisamira83/LSAHR_dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: "Large-Scale Arabic Hotel Review Dataset for Personalized Recommendation" — an academic dataset of Arabic-language hotel reviews (source platform and date coverage not confirmed by inspection; repo updated Jun 2026, custom/other licence).
candidates.why_useful: Potential MENA-region hotel-demand text source, a geography with almost no coverage in our current holdings; value depends entirely on whether reviews carry dates and which platform/cities are covered, which was not verified.

candidates.name: apify/keboola-gmrs
candidates.what_it_holds: Keboola-platform connector/extractor wrapping the Apify Google Maps Reviews Scraper actor (0 stars, MIT). Thin integration glue, not a scraper itself and no data.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal — only useful if the team already runs Keboola pipelines; otherwise the direct scrapers above are more useful.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: subset of the google-maps-reviews-scraper tools already listed

notes: This theme is dominated on GitHub by two unhelpful clusters: (1) hundreds of near-identical student notebooks re-analysing the single well-known Kaggle TripAdvisor/Booking.com hotel-review CSV (excluded per instructions, confirmed by first search returning ~40 such repos with 0-3 stars each), and (2) dozens of near-identical 'Google Maps reviews scraper' repos, mostly thin wrappers around Apify actors or Selenium/Playwright boilerplate with near-zero stars — only the two most-starred, actively maintained ones were kept. Direct queries for 'review velocity nowcast tourism' and 'review count nowcasting economic activity' returned zero results — this specific nowcasting-methodology niche does not appear to be represented as a named GitHub project; it likely lives inside academic-paper repos not indexed under these terms, or would need `gh search code` (not used, to conserve the 10/min budget) to find by import/algorithm rather than title. The standout find is HotelRec (50M dated TripAdvisor reviews) which is meaningfully larger and differently-sourced than the Booking.com/RecTour24 data already held, though its licence is academic-only and it looks like a static historical crawl rather than a live feed. WebSearch tool was unavailable (session-wide budget exhausted by other agents) for the back-half of this scout, limiting cross-checking beyond gh CLI and direct WebFetch of the one most-promising repo's README. Given the rate-limit budget (6 gh search calls), broader review-velocity-nowcast method repos (MIDAS/DFM applied to reviews specifically) were not separately searched and would be a reasonable next scout to run under the 'methods_tooling' theme instead of this one.
